correctness.rationale: Transitivity leaves exactly the bottom, three singleton-edge states and top. Up to restriction to these states the eight nonconstant upper sets are generated by choosing a subset of singleton-edge states and including the top. Nested covariances are nonnegative; the three incomparable types give q-p², q(1+p)-2p², and p-(2p-q)². The middle inequality gives q≥2p²/(1+p)≥p² and 0≤2p-q≤2p/(1+p), proving the other signs even at p=0 or 1. Finite layer-cake expansion then handles all increasing functions. Asai–Kubo–Kuo Theorem 1 gives q/p²≤n/(n-1) and monotonicity of B_(n-1)/B_n, so the witness is negative for n≥4 using p≤1/3, and is -1/25 at n=3. Strict q>p² is the variance of 1/M in the nondegenerate Stam mixture. Also p≤203/877<1/4 for n≥7 makes p-(2p-q)²>0; exact substitution at n=3,4,5,6 gives 1/25, 11/225, 155/2704, 2635/41209. Exactly three incomparable disjoint (1,2) event pairs give the negative type. Graph contraction, rank subadditivity and the positive covariance of two strictly decreasing functions of M prove the principal-event claim. The seating ratios and simple substitution verify the Pitman–Yor numerator α(1-α)(θ+α), including the Ewens equality boundary; fixed colors instead give -(m-1)/m³. These are analytic checks on the full ranges; submitted verify.py was inspected, not executed. The association criterion is only for the three tagged coordinates, not an iff for all edges.

evidence: The earlier conditional probability is E[1_C_F | M]=M^{-r(F)} for any edge set F. Combined with r(F∪H)≤r(F)+r(H) and a nondegenerate M this implies strict positive covariance of nonempty principal events, hence of individual edge indicators. The seating rule directly determines p,q.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The conditional rank formula covers the principal-event subclaim but does not by monotonicity imply a negative covariance for a disjunctive event or the complete iff. The substantive novelty is the threshold and simultaneous contrast; the model trichotomy follows once that threshold is proved.

evidence: The graph-indexed Ewens–Pitman finding concerns coordinate-exchangeability and the triangle extension horizon. The fixed-block-count finding concerns spanning-tree edge-count covariance. Neither compares increasing events in the five-state triangle support.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Symmetry, extendibility, and pairwise covariance are not equivalent to association. The disjoint singleton-versus-two-event test is stronger than pairwise tests, even with all five-state probabilities known.

value.rationale: The criterion locates precisely why natural tests for clustering dependence can disagree. Under the canonical uniform partition law, every principal requirement is positively correlated but a disjunction on only three tags supplies a strict obstruction for all n≥3. The threshold distinguishes the fixed-color, Ewens boundary and positive-discount cases without merely retesting pairwise correlations. This is useful without claiming an iff for all coalescence indicators on larger sets.
